story.logline: Start at the outer skin of a cell and open each gate as you walk inward to the nucleus.

restoredLine.text: Look, the pore is turning! Every gate you fixed is helping it.

approach.text: This bit of membrane froze solid. One of these three pods holds a Mimic, and it's lying.

instruction.text: Push the probe into the membrane, then catch the pod that's lying.

tutorial.text: Turn the depth dial to move the needle. My readouts show what the membrane is like at the tip.

insight.text: Healthy membrane moves aside for the needle and closes behind it. Only the frozen ridge stays stiff.

hints.text: Watch the heads while the needle goes in. See if they bend and flow, or stay stiff.
The membrane is fat molecules with oily tails. Oil doesn't hold a stiff shape, so it flows around the needle.
The pod about the oily middle blocking ions is true. Compare the other two.

default.text: That pod's claim was true. Push the needle in again and watch how the heads move.

success.text: Right! The membrane is a thin film that flows. Proteins in it work as doors.

payoffLine.text: Got the Mimic! Look, the stiff ridge is melting into a path.

approach.text: Molecules are lining up at Gate 2. Careful with the small ones.

instruction.text: Send each molecule down the Oil Road or through the Crossing Gate's ring.

tutorial.text: Pick a molecule, then pick a lane. Nothing crosses until every molecule has a lane.

insight.text: The oily middle of the membrane does the blocking. The heads just sit on top.

hints.text: Na+ and Cl- are tiny, but size won't pick their lane. Pip's lens shows which ones carry water.
Check each molecule for a charge, like the + on Na+. The Oil Road pushes charged ones away.
The steroid is the one people get wrong. Check if it's charged or made from fat.

default.text: One molecule got turned away. Check for a charge before you check its size.

line.text: Size fooled you there. Even a tiny ion bounces off the oil.
Size isn't what the oil checks. A molecule made from fat slips through, even a big one.

success.text: Oily molecules slip through the oil. Charged and polar ones need a protein door, even tiny ones.

payoffLine.text: Every molecule took the right lane. The Crossing Gate is spinning up!

approach.text: The Balance Lock opens when both sides of this tank are even. Right now the dye is piled up on the left.

instruction.text: Set the dye load and watch the tank, then catch the pod that's lying.

tutorial.text: The dye dial refills the left side. On my top readout, white is the left side and green is the right.

insight.text: See the tracer with the white ring? It wanders and doubles back all the time.

hints.text: Follow the tracer with the white ring. Does it ever seem to know where the empty side is?
Each particle moves at random. More start on the crowded side, so more happen to cross from there.
The pod about particles bumping at random is true. Compare the other two.

default.text: That pod's story matched the tank. Watch the tracer's path for a bit, then try again.

success.text: Yes! The particles just move at random. That random spreading is called diffusion.

payoffLine.text: Mimic caught! The tank is evening out, and the Balance Lock is opening.

approach.text: There's a test cell in a salt bath, and our raft is stuck in a dry lock. It won't float until something crosses.

instruction.text: Add salt to the bath and watch the test cell, then catch the pod that's lying.

tutorial.text: The salt dial sets the bath. Below 2% the pods go quiet, because their claims are about a salty bath.

insight.text: Those salt cubes keep bouncing off the cell. The membrane is picky about what it lets in.

hints.text: Two things could cross, the water or the salt. Only one of them gets through the membrane.
Water moves toward the side with more salt. Watch where the blue droplets go.
The pod about the cell shrinking is true. Compare the other two.

default.text: That pod was honest. Turn the salt up and down, and watch what the white salt cubes do.

success.text: Yes! The salt stays put and the water moves toward it. That's called osmosis.

payoffLine.text: Caught it! Now I'm salting the raft lock, so water will flow in and float you up.

approach.text: Mm, visitors. I'm Poro, and I only let water through.
Cells are drifting down the canal. Each lock needs a label before its cell floats past.

instruction.text: Label each lock's bath before its cell drifts past.

tutorial.text: You get eight seconds per cell at the Label Lock. A cell that floats past with no label counts as a miss.

insight.text: The dots show how much salt is dissolved, both in the bath and in the cell.

hints.text: Each label is about the bath around the cell. Compare the dots outside with the dots inside.
Hyper means more dots outside, so water leaves. Hypo means fewer, so water comes in.
The cell in pure water is the one people mix up. Pure water has almost no dots.

default.text: One label doesn't fit its bath. Compare the dots inside that cell with the dots around it.

line.text: Hyper means more stuff dissolved, so less water. A bath of nearly pure water has the fewest dots.

success.text: Right! Tonicity compares the bath with the cell, and that tells you which way water goes.

payoffLine.text: The canal is draining! Steps are coming up out of the water. That's our way up.

after.text: Well sorted. Here, take my notebook. It's a bit damp.

approach.text: Two gates guard the pump room. The Pump Gate burns ATP, the cell's energy fuel.

instruction.text: Send each cargo to the Glide Gate if it moves for free, or the Pump Gate if it costs ATP.

tutorial.text: Each cargo floats over its own ramp. The thick end of the ramp is the crowded side.

insight.text: There are lots of proteins here, and most of them never use any ATP.

hints.text: Look at the glucose. It rides a carrier protein, but check the slope under it.
Check if each cargo rolls down its slope or gets pushed up. Only pushing up costs ATP.
Water through its channel often lands at the wrong gate. Ask if anything has to push it.

default.text: One cargo went to the wrong gate. Check if it rolls down its slope or gets pushed up.

line.text: Using a protein doesn't mean paying energy. Cargo going downhill rides through for free.

success.text: That's it. A protein can help for free, and energy only gets spent going uphill.

payoffLine.text: The gate's open and the Carrier Door is turning. Everybody in!

approach.text: Two tanks, one high and one low, with a pump between them. Three pods argue about what the pump does.

instruction.text: Feed the pump some ATP and watch the tanks, then catch the pod that's lying.

tutorial.text: The ATP dial feeds the pump. On my readouts, white is the high tank and green is the low one.

insight.text: With no ATP, the gap between the tanks drains away. That's why this cell is shutting down.

hints.text: Look at the pod about ATP. Set the feed to zero and ask why a cell would pay to move things.
Things drift from the high tank to the low one for free. Paying ATP only makes sense the other way.
The pod about ATP is true. Compare the other two.

default.text: That pod told the truth. Turn the feed to zero, then back up, and watch the gap between the tanks.

success.text: Right! A pump pushes things uphill, from low to high, and ATP pays for every push.

payoffLine.text: That's the Mimic! The lanterns are on and the lift has power.

approach.text: There it is, the sodium-potassium pump. It's the biggest machine on this membrane, and someone pulled its cables.

instruction.text: Rewire the pump by plugging each socket into the right cartridge.

tutorial.text: Each cartridge loads what its label says. Turn the stage dial to run one cycle and test it.

insight.text: Every nerve signal starts with this pump. The charge readout shows what one cycle leaves behind.

hints.text: Look at the counts for sodium and potassium. They aren't the same number.
Sodium goes out and potassium comes in. More ions leave than come in each cycle.
One of the 'out' cartridges is a trap. Only sodium leaves, and the counts aren't equal.

default.text: The pump jammed partway. Find the socket with the wrong cartridge and try another one.

line.text: Two out and two in doesn't move any charge. The charge needle didn't budge.

success.text: Right! Three out and two in leaves the inside a bit negative. That's what lets nerves fire.

payoffLine.text: It's running, over and over! The Hall Gate is lifting.

approach.text: Four cells are coming down the canal, and our barge is stuck in the mud.

instruction.text: Set each lock's valve to the way water moves before its cell drifts past.

tutorial.text: Hover over a valve to see arrows for its flow. You get eight seconds per cell.

insight.text: The salt dots never leave their side of the membrane. Only the water moves.

hints.text: Compare the dots inside each cell with the dots in the water around it.
Water moves toward the side with more dots. The dots themselves stay put.
The potato is easy to get wrong. Its syrup is packed with far more sugar than the potato.

default.text: One flow was wrong. The salt stays put, so check which side the water heads to.

line.text: The salt never crosses. Watch the dots stay put, and follow the water instead.

success.text: Nice. Find the side with more dots, and that's where the water goes.

payoffLine.text: All correct! The locks are filling, and the barge is rising.

approach.text: No gate in this cell is big enough for our sub. So the membrane is going to swallow us, on purpose.

instruction.text: Put the stage plates in the order that gets us into the cell. One plate doesn't belong.

tutorial.text: The playback dial runs the membrane through your plates, one slot at a time. Turn it to watch each step.

insight.text: Nothing this big fits through a protein. The membrane has to carry it, and that costs ATP.

hints.text: Start with our sub outside the cell. Nothing can happen until it touches the membrane.
The membrane has to wrap around us before it can close the pocket.
Once the pocket pinches off, we're inside a bubble. What happens to that bubble last?

default.text: The lift got stuck partway. Play back your plates and find the step that can't happen yet.

line.text: Hold. The membrane can't do that yet.
Nothing this big dissolves through us. The membrane has to carry it.

success.text: We were too big for a protein, so the membrane wrapped us up. That's called endocytosis.

payoffLine.text: We're folding in... pinching off... and we're in! Welcome inside the cell, Diver.

instruction.text: Feed each cargo to the maw that matches how it crosses the membrane.

tutorial.text: Cargo comes in three batches. My ATP readout shows what the Pump Maw costs.

insight.text: Every crossing comes down to two things. Which way is it going, and can it pass through oil?

hints.text: Check the slope under each cargo first. It shows which way that one is moving.
Anything pushed uphill goes to the Pump Maw. If it's downhill, ask if it can slip through oil.
Water is the tricky one. Check if it goes through a protein.

default.text: One came back. Check which way it's going first, then whether oil lets it through.

success.text: Oil lets small nonpolar things through. Proteins help the rest, and only uphill trips cost ATP.

payoffLine.text: Hrrm. All sorted right. You may pass.

line.text: Two cargo first. Show me which roll and which get pushed.
Two more. My Pump Maw is hungry, and it hates waste.
The last three. Get these right and the vault opens.

fail.text: Hrrm. That one came back. Check which way it's going.
My maws don't argue, they spit. Check the slope under that one.

line.text: A door costs nothing. My Pump Maw won't pay for downhill trips.
Only downhill? Then how does my Pump Maw climb all day?
Small won't get you in. Charged things sink in my oil.

plaques.title: Heads and Tails
plaques.text: Each fat molecule has a head that likes water and two tails that don't. The tails hide inside, and the heads face out.

plaques.title: Why Oil Says No
plaques.text: Charged things like to have water around them. The membrane's oily middle has none, so ions get turned away.

lines.text: You are on the outside of a living cell. Its gates have stopped, and the cell is running down.
The hull is holding and everyone's dry. Welcome to the outside of a living cell, Diver.
We've shrunk! That shiny film ahead is the membrane, the cell's thin skin.
Bad news. The pumps and gates have stopped, so we can't get inside yet.
A cell needs its inside to be different from its outside. If they end up the same, the cell stops working.
Good news. Every gate here is a machine, and machines can be restarted.
Get every gate running again and we'll reach the nucleus. That's the cell's control center.
Pip goes with you, and I'll stay with the sub. ...Pip says hello.
The Gradient Meter reads twelve percent. Pip will blink at anything worth a closer look.
I have pumped for a billion years. Show me you know what costs energy.
Feed each cargo to the right maw. Waste my ATP and the vault stays shut.
The pore is turning. Go, and tell the nucleus the pumps are running again.
We made it to the nucleus! You knew what could cross each gate, and how.
The Gradient Meter is at a hundred percent. Inside and outside are different again, so the cell can live.
Oxygen slips through the oil, and glucose rides a carrier. Sodium gets pumped uphill with ATP.
Bring Pip home, Diver. And, um... the cell next door looks a little still, too.
